```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)

source(here::here("R", "02b_extend_panel_2526.R"))

INK    <- "#1a1a2e"
PURPLE <- "#361a54"
BRIGHT <- "#993bff"
WARM   <- "#f56300"
GREY   <- "#666688"

theme_note <- function(base = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", colour = PURPLE),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = GREY, size = rel(0.9)),
      axis.title       = element_text(colour = GREY, size = rel(0.9)),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}

p5_path <- here::here("data", "panel_data_5yr.rds")
p5 <- if (file.exists(p5_path)) readRDS(p5_path) else extend_panel_2526()

# The EES institution-level file carries 2023/24 to 2025/26, so year-on-year
# comparisons are made inside it rather than against the panel, whose 2024/25
# came from the provisional performance tables.
e25 <- ees_ks4_year(202425L)
e26 <- ees_ks4_year(202526L)

yoy <- inner_join(
  e25 |> select(URN, SCHNAME, LANAME, a25 = ATT8SCR, d25 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
                n25 = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A),
  e26 |> select(URN, a26 = ATT8SCR, d26 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
                n26 = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, f26 = PTFSM6CLA1A),
  by = "URN") |>
  mutate(chg = a26 - a25, chg_dis = d26 - d25, chg_ndis = n26 - n25)

fmt <- function(x, d = 2) sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f"), x)

# Brighton Aldridge Community Academy is BACA everywhere it is shown. The
# data keeps its full name, so this is applied at the point of display.
shorten <- function(x) {
  x <- sub("^Brighton Aldridge.*", "BACA", x)
  sub(" School$| High School$| Community Academy$| and Sixth Form Centre$", "", x)
}
```

::: callout-important
## Provisional. Confirmable in February 2027.

The 2025/26 Key Stage 4 figures are **provisional**, published by the
Department for Education on 15 October 2026 and based on results before
schools' amendment requests have been applied. The **revised figures follow
in February 2027**, and that is the point at which anything here can be
confirmed.

That matters more than usual for this particular year. The most noticeable finding
below rests on a single school's single cohort moving a long way out of line
— and a single year that far out of line is exactly the case where a revision
bites hardest. **Nothing here should be treated as settled until February.**

The second date worth holding on to is **2026/27**, the first Key Stage 4 year
with a real Key Stage 2 baseline again. Until then every value-added figure
for 2024/25 and 2025/26 — here and in anyone else's analysis — rests on a
carried-forward intake score. See §6.4.
:::

::: callout-note
## An addendum, not a revision

This is a **standalone addendum** to
[*How to Pull the Right Lever*](pulling_the_right_lever_v2.html). That report
is unchanged and still stands on its own four years of data: nothing here has
been folded back into it, and every figure it publishes still reproduces from
`data/panel_data.rds` exactly as before. The five-year panel this note uses is
written separately, to `data/panel_data_5yr.rds`.
:::

# What arrived, and why the pipeline had to change

The 2025/26 release brings a fifth year of Key Stage 4 results. It also
brings the end of the route this project used to get them.

> "Compare school and college performance (CSCP) will close soon. From autumn
> 2026, you will be able to use a new service. Data on CSCP will not be
> updated past the 2024/25 academic year."

`R/00_download_cscp.R` can therefore fetch 2021/22 to 2024/25 and nothing
after it. It is kept exactly as it is, because every published figure for
those four years reproduces from the files it fetched. From 2025/26 the data
comes instead from Explore Education Statistics, through
`R/00b_download_ees_api.R`, and is shaped into a panel year by
`R/01b_extract_ees_2526.R`.

Three things are genuinely absent from the new year, and all three are carried
as explicit gaps rather than quietly filled:

| Missing | Why | Consequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Progress 8** | The 2025/26 cohort has no Key Stage 2 baseline — the 2019/20 and 2020/21 primary assessments were cancelled, and DfE confirmed no replacement measure | Already true of 2024/25; the reduced "core" specification was built for exactly this |
| **Prior attainment** | Same cause | `PTPRIORLO` / `PTPRIORHI` are `NA`, as in 2024/25 |
| **Full-year absence** | 2025/26 full-year absence publishes around March 2027 | Handled below — and it is the one that mattered |

# Is the new source the same as the old one?

The EES institution-level file covers 2023/24 to 2025/26, so it overlaps the
panel by two years. If the mapping from the EES long format onto the panel's
column names is right, the overlap should agree.

```{r validate}
#| tbl-cap: "EES institution-level data against the CSCP performance tables, on the years both cover"
panel4 <- readRDS(here::here("data", "panel_data.rds")) |>
  mutate(URN = as.character(URN))

cmp <- function(tp, ay) {
  e <- ees_ks4_year(tp) |>
    select(URN, e_att8 = ATT8SCR, e_dis = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
           e_ndis = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, e_fsm = PTFSM6CLA1A)
  p <- panel4 |> filter(academic_year == ay) |>
    select(URN, p_att8 = ATT8SCR, p_dis = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
           p_ndis = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, p_fsm = PTFSM6CLA1A)
  d <- inner_join(e, p, by = "URN")
  purrr::map_dfr(
    c(att8 = "Attainment 8", dis = "Disadvantaged",
      ndis = "Not disadvantaged", fsm = "Disadvantaged share"),
    function(lab) {
      v <- names(which(c(att8 = "Attainment 8", dis = "Disadvantaged",
                         ndis = "Not disadvantaged",
                         fsm = "Disadvantaged share") == lab))
      a <- d[[paste0("e_", v)]]; b <- d[[paste0("p_", v)]]
      ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b)
      tibble(Year = ay, Measure = lab, Schools = sum(ok),
             r = round(cor(a[ok], b[ok]), 4),
             `Mean difference` = round(mean(a[ok] - b[ok]), 3),
             `Agree exactly` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(abs(a[ok] - b[ok]) < 0.05)))
    })
}

bind_rows(cmp(202324L, "2023-2024"), cmp(202425L, "2024-2025"))
```

It does: correlations of 0.9998 to 1.0000 on every measure. The mapping is
sound.

The second row group is the more interesting one. For 2023/24 the two sources
agree exactly for about nine schools in ten; for 2024/25 only about three in
ten, with the EES figures running a shade higher. That is not an error — it is
the **provisional-to-revised revision**. The panel's 2024/25 came from
`england_ks4provisional.csv`; the EES file now carries the revised figures,
which include late results and the amendments schools requested. The same
thing will happen to the 2025/26 numbers in February 2027.

# The absence problem, and what to do about it

Absence is the strongest single predictor in the Lever model, and the centre
of its argument. Full-year absence for 2025/26 does not exist yet.

What does exist is a school-level file running **2016/17 to 2025/26** covering
the **autumn and spring terms** — every year of the panel, on one consistent
basis, reaching the new year. Summer term absence is excluded, so it is a
different quantity from `PERCTOT` and is carried as a separate variable,
`PERCTOT_2term`, never joined onto the old one.

```{r absence-compare}
#| fig-cap: "Full-year and autumn+spring absence, for the school-years where both are published"
both <- p5 |> filter(!is.na(PERCTOT), !is.na(PERCTOT_2term))
r_abs <- cor(both$PERCTOT, both$PERCTOT_2term)
d_abs <- mean(both$PERCTOT_2term - both$PERCTOT)

ggplot(both, aes(PERCTOT, PERCTOT_2term)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linetype = "31") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.12, colour = PURPLE, size = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Overall absence, full academic year (%)",
       y = "Overall absence, autumn + spring (%)",
       title = "The two absence bases measure nearly the same thing",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s school-years, r = %.3f, autumn+spring running %.2f points lower on average",
                          format(nrow(both), big.mark = ","), r_abs, d_abs)) +
  theme_note()
```

They are close: `r sprintf("r = %.3f", r_abs)` across
`r format(nrow(both), big.mark = ",")` school-years, with the two-term figure
`r sprintf("%.2f", abs(d_abs))` percentage points lower on average — summer
term absence is the higher part of the year, so dropping it pulls the number
down slightly and almost uniformly.

# Does the conclusion survive?

The question worth asking is not "can a fifth year be added" but "does adding
it change the answer". Three fits separate the two things that could move the
result — the change of absence basis, and the extra year.

```{r fits}
#| cache: true
fit_core <- function(d, absvar) {
  d <- d |>
    filter(!is.na(ATT8SCR), ATT8SCR > 0,
           !is.na(.data[[absvar]]), .data[[absvar]] > 0,
           !is.na(PTFSM6CLA1A), PTFSM6CLA1A > 0,
           !is.na(PNUMEAL), PNUMEAL > 0,
           !is.na(ADMPOL_PT), !is.na(gorard_segregation),
           !is.na(OFSTEDRATING_1), !is.na(gor_name), !is.na(LANAME))
  f <- as.formula(sprintf(paste(
    "log(ATT8SCR) ~ log(PTFSM6CLA1A) + log(%s) + log(PNUMEAL) +",
    "ADMPOL_PT + gorard_segregation +",
    "(1 | year_label) + (1 | OFSTEDRATING_1) + (1 | gor_name/LANAME)"), absvar))
  m <- lmer(f, data = d, REML = TRUE,
            control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
                                  optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
  list(m = m, n = nrow(d), co = summary(m)$coefficients)
}

four <- filter(p5, academic_year != "2025-2026")
A <- fit_core(four, "PERCTOT")
B <- fit_core(four, "PERCTOT_2term")
C <- fit_core(p5,   "PERCTOT_2term")

pull <- function(r, pat) {
  rn <- grep(pat, rownames(r$co), value = TRUE)[1]
  c(est = r$co[rn, "Estimate"], se = r$co[rn, "Std. Error"])
}
```

```{r fits-table}
#| tbl-cap: "The core specification, fitted three ways"
tibble(
  Fit = c("A. Published baseline", "B. Absence basis swapped", "C. Fifth year added"),
  Years = c("2021/22–2024/25", "2021/22–2024/25", "2021/22–2025/26"),
  Absence = c("Full year", "Autumn + spring", "Autumn + spring"),
  `School-years` = format(c(A$n, B$n, C$n), big.mark = ","),
  `Absence coefficient` = sprintf("%.4f", c(pull(A, "PERCTOT")["est"],
                                            pull(B, "PERCTOT")["est"],
                                            pull(C, "PERCTOT")["est"])),
  `Disadvantage coefficient` = sprintf("%.4f", c(pull(A, "PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"],
                                                 pull(B, "PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"],
                                                 pull(C, "PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"]))
)
```

```{r coef-plot}
#| fig-cap: "Absence and disadvantage coefficients across the three fits, with 95% intervals"
#| fig-height: 3.4
fits  <- list(`A. Published\nbaseline` = A,
              `B. Absence basis\nswapped` = B,
              `C. Fifth year\nadded` = C)
terms <- c(Absence = "PERCTOT", Disadvantage = "PTFSM6CLA1A")

cf <- purrr::map_dfr(names(terms), function(tm) {
  purrr::map_dfr(names(fits), function(fn) {
    v <- pull(fits[[fn]], terms[[tm]])
    tibble(fit = fn, term = tm, est = unname(v["est"]), se = unname(v["se"]))
  })
}) |>
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = names(fits)))

ggplot(cf, aes(est, fit, colour = term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linetype = "31") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = est - 1.96 * se, xmax = est + 1.96 * se),
                 height = 0.16, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Absence = BRIGHT, Disadvantage = WARM),
                      guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ term, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Coefficient on log(x) in log(Attainment 8)", y = NULL,
       title = "Neither change moves the result",
       subtitle = "Elasticities: a 10% rise in absence costs about 2.6% of Attainment 8") +
  theme_note(12)
```

The absence elasticity goes
**`r sprintf("%.4f", pull(A,"PERCTOT")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(B,"PERCTOT")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(C,"PERCTOT")["est"])`**.
The disadvantage elasticity goes
**`r sprintf("%.4f", pull(A,"PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(B,"PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(C,"PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"])`**.

Every one of those moves is far inside the standard errors. Swapping the
absence basis is close to free, and a fifth year of data leaves the central
finding exactly where it was: **absence carries roughly twice the weight of
disadvantage**, and it is the variable policy has most purchase on.

That is the most useful thing a new year of data can do. It was a chance for
the conclusion to fail, and it did not.

# What actually changed in 2025/26

```{r england}
# Paired means only: a school missing either year would otherwise shift the
# two averages by different amounts and invent a change that is not there.
nat_all <- yoy |> filter(!is.na(a25), !is.na(a26))
nat_dis <- yoy |> filter(!is.na(d25), !is.na(d26), !is.na(n25), !is.na(n26))
nat <- tibble(
  n   = nrow(nat_all),
  a25 = mean(nat_all$a25), a26 = mean(nat_all$a26),
  d25 = mean(nat_dis$d25), d26 = mean(nat_dis$d26),
  n25 = mean(nat_dis$n25), n26 = mean(nat_dis$n26))
gap25 <- nat$n25 - nat$d25; gap26 <- nat$n26 - nat$d26
```

Across `r format(nat$n, big.mark = ",")` matched state-funded mainstream
schools in England, headline Attainment 8 was **flat**: a change of
`r fmt(nat$a26 - nat$a25)` points. Underneath it, something more interesting:

- disadvantaged pupils **`r fmt(nat$d26 - nat$d25)`**, from `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$d25)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$d26)`
- everyone else **`r fmt(nat$n26 - nat$n25)`**, from `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$n25)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$n26)`
- the **disadvantage gap narrowed by `r sprintf("%.2f", gap25 - gap26)` points**, from `r sprintf("%.2f", gap25)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", gap26)`

A flat headline hiding a narrowing gap is precisely the pattern a measure
built on averages is bad at showing, and precisely the one that matters.

## Brighton and Hove

```{r brighton}
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton and Hove state-funded secondary schools, 2024/25 to 2025/26 (provisional)"
bh <- yoy |>
  filter(LANAME == "Brighton and Hove", !is.na(f26)) |>
  arrange(desc(chg)) |>
  transmute(School = shorten(SCHNAME),
            `A8 2024/25` = a25, `A8 2025/26` = a26, Change = chg,
            `Disadvantaged 2024/25` = d25, `Disadvantaged 2025/26` = d26,
            `Disadvantaged change` = chg_dis,
            `Disadvantaged %` = f26)
bh
```

The city moved **`r fmt(mean(bh$Change, na.rm = TRUE))` points** against a
national change of `r fmt(nat$a26 - nat$a25)`. Two movements stand out, and
they are in opposite directions: Longhill High School, and Brighton Aldridge
Community Academy — **BACA** from here on.

::: callout-note
Both of those movements are smaller than they look here. Attainment 8 is a
mean over every pupil on roll, entered or not, and the entry rates at these
two schools moved sharply in opposite directions. §7 measures the same years
on the pupils who were actually entered; read it before quoting either
figure.
:::

```{r lh-baca}
#| fig-cap: "Longhill and BACA, against the national distribution of Attainment 8"
pctile <- function(v, x) 100 * mean(v <= x, na.rm = TRUE)
lh <- yoy |> filter(SCHNAME == "Longhill High School")
bc <- yoy |> filter(SCHNAME == "Brighton Aldridge Community Academy")

mk <- tibble(
  school = rep(c("Longhill", "BACA"), each = 2),
  year   = rep(c("2024/25", "2025/26"), 2),
  a8     = c(lh$a25, lh$a26, bc$a25, bc$a26))

ggplot(yoy |> select(a26) |> filter(!is.na(a26)), aes(a26)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(data = mk, aes(xintercept = a8, colour = school,
                            linetype = year), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Longhill = BRIGHT,
                                 `BACA` = WARM)) +
  labs(x = "Attainment 8, 2025/26", y = "Schools", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       title = "Longhill up, BACA down — they have crossed",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste(
         "Longhill %.1f to %.1f, rising past %.0f%% to %.0f%% of schools in England;",
         "BACA %.1f to %.1f, falling from above %.0f%% to above %.0f%%"),
         lh$a25, lh$a26, pctile(yoy$a25, lh$a25), pctile(yoy$a26, lh$a26),
         bc$a25, bc$a26, pctile(yoy$a25, bc$a25), pctile(yoy$a26, bc$a26))) +
  theme_note()
```

**Longhill rose `r fmt(lh$chg, 1)` points** and its disadvantaged pupils rose
`r fmt(lh$chg_dis, 1)`. **BACA fell `r fmt(bc$chg, 1)`**, with its
disadvantaged pupils falling `r fmt(bc$chg_dis, 1)`. On the headline measure
the two schools have swapped places.

## Did BACA simply take a harder intake?

That is the first thing to rule out, and the answer is no — the composition
moved the other way.

```{r composition}
#| tbl-cap: "Cohort composition and scores, three years"
comp <- bind_rows(
  ees_ks4_year(202324L) |> mutate(Year = "2023/24"),
  e25 |> mutate(Year = "2024/25"),
  e26 |> mutate(Year = "2025/26")) |>
  filter(SCHNAME %in% c("Longhill High School",
                        "Brighton Aldridge Community Academy")) |>
  transmute(School = ifelse(grepl("Aldridge", SCHNAME),
                            "BACA", "Longhill"),
            Year, Cohort = TPUP,
            `Disadvantaged %` = PTFSM6CLA1A,
            `A8 all` = ATT8SCR,
            `A8 disadvantaged` = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
            `A8 not disadvantaged` = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A) |>
  mutate(`Internal gap` = `A8 not disadvantaged` - `A8 disadvantaged`) |>
  arrange(School, Year)
comp
```

```{r baca-numbers}
b25 <- comp |> filter(School == "BACA", Year == "2024/25")
b26 <- comp |> filter(School == "BACA", Year == "2025/26")
l25 <- comp |> filter(School == "Longhill", Year == "2024/25")
l26 <- comp |> filter(School == "Longhill", Year == "2025/26")

# How far outside the normal range is a move of that size, for a
# disadvantaged cohort of that size?
nat_dis <- inner_join(
  e25 |> select(URN, SCHNAME, d25 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A),
  e26 |> select(URN, d26 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A, t26 = TFSM6CLA1A),
  by = "URN") |>
  filter(!is.na(d25), !is.na(d26)) |>
  mutate(chg = d26 - d25)
bc_chg <- nat_dis$chg[nat_dis$SCHNAME == "Brighton Aldridge Community Academy"]
peer <- nat_dis |> filter(!is.na(t26), t26 >= 60, t26 < 80)
```

BACA's cohort **grew**, from `r b25$Cohort` to `r b26$Cohort`,
and its disadvantaged share **fell**, from
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", b25[["Disadvantaged %"]])` to
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", b26[["Disadvantaged %"]])`. A smaller disadvantaged share
should push the headline score *up*. Its non-disadvantaged pupils also did
better, `r sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", b25[["A8 not disadvantaged"]], b26[["A8 not disadvantaged"]])`.

The headline fell anyway, because the disadvantaged half of the school fell
`r sprintf("%.1f", abs(bc_chg))` points. **The gap between the two groups
inside the school went from `r sprintf("%.1f", b25[["Internal gap"]])` points
to `r sprintf("%.1f", b26[["Internal gap"]])`** in a single year.

Longhill moved in the opposite direction on every line: disadvantaged share
down from `r sprintf("%.1f%%", l25[["Disadvantaged %"]])` to
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", l26[["Disadvantaged %"]])`, both groups up, and its
internal gap narrowing from `r sprintf("%.1f", l25[["Internal gap"]])` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", l26[["Internal gap"]])`.

```{r peer-check}
#| fig-cap: "Year-on-year change in disadvantaged Attainment 8, schools with 60-79 disadvantaged pupils"
#| fig-height: 3.2
ggplot(peer, aes(chg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 45, fill = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = bc_chg, colour = WARM, linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = bc_chg, y = Inf, label = "  BACA",
           colour = WARM, hjust = 0, vjust = 1.6, size = 3.6) +
  labs(x = "Change in disadvantaged Attainment 8, 2024/25 to 2025/26",
       y = "Schools",
       title = "Not the ordinary noise of a small cohort",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s schools with a disadvantaged cohort the same size as BACA's; SD %.1f points, %.0f%% move more than 10",
                          format(nrow(peer), big.mark = ","), sd(peer$chg),
                          100 * mean(abs(peer$chg) > 10))) +
  theme_note(12)
```

Small cohorts do swing. But for schools with a disadvantaged cohort the size
of BACA's, the standard deviation of year-on-year change is
`r sprintf("%.1f", sd(peer$chg))` points and only
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(abs(peer$chg) > 10))` move by more than ten.
BACA's `r sprintf("%.1f", bc_chg)` sits at the
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(nat_dis$chg <= bc_chg))`th percentile of all
`r format(nrow(nat_dis), big.mark = ",")` schools nationally. Whatever it is,
it is not the usual noise.

::: callout-warning
## Do not over-read this yet

Three reasons for caution, all of them real:

1. **These are provisional figures.** February's revisions will move them.
2. **One year.** The composition check above rules out the easy explanation,
   and the peer comparison rules out ordinary small-cohort noise — but a
   single cohort can still be unusual for reasons no published table shows.
   The thing to do is look again in February, and again in 2027.
3. **Attainment 8 is not value added.** The simulator's third policy lever —
   "what if Longhill added value like BACA" — rests on a
   four-year value-added measure, not on one year of headline scores. A
   single year's Attainment 8 cannot overturn it.

What this *does* justify is re-running the value-added measure with the new
year in it, and seeing whether the gap that lever depends on is still there.
:::

# The value-added measure, re-run

Attainment 8 describes an intake. The measure the Brighton work leans on is
**value added** — what a school adds once its intake is accounted for. In
*How to Pull the Right Lever* it is the residual of the fitted model:
observed Attainment 8 minus what the model expects, school by school and year
by year, for **three pupil groups separately** — all pupils, disadvantaged,
and non-disadvantaged. All three are carried into the new year here, because
a comparison between them is most of the point.

The model behind it is the **imputed full specification** — nine predictors
including prior attainment and three workforce terms — not the reduced core
one. So the right way to add a fifth year is to **predict from the published
models**, not to refit. Refitting moves all four published years; predicting
leaves them untouched and puts 2025/26 on the same yardstick.

::: callout-note
## A back-transformation that used to be done two ways, now reconciled

Checking this against the published league tables turned up an
inconsistency in the project itself, since fixed.

The models are fitted on $\log(\text{ATT8SCR})$, so $\exp(\hat{y})$ is the
conditional **median**. The expected score given a school's intake is
$\exp(\hat{y})\cdot\exp(\sigma^2/2)$. `safe_predict()` applied that
correction, writing `residual_ATT8SCR_imputed` into the panel and from there
into the simulator's value-added scenario. The league tables and the
observed-versus-predicted figure in the main report did not, and so printed
residuals about **0.2 Attainment 8 points higher** for the same school and
year.

The report now uses the corrected form, through one shared helper, so the two
cannot drift apart again. Both league tables match `residual_*_imputed`
exactly. What moved: every residual falls by about 0.2 points — not uniformly,
since the correction is multiplicative on the predicted value, so it ranges
0.11 to 0.43 across the national range. Rankings are almost untouched
(Spearman 0.9999); in the Brighton tables only King's and Hove Park swap, at
ranks 6 and 7 of the disadvantaged table, where they were tied at 0.9.

Everything below uses the corrected form.
:::

```{r va-fit}
#| cache: true
#| output: false
source(here::here("R", "05b_value_added_2526.R"))
va    <- value_added_5yr(p5, convention = "corrected", verify = FALSE)
vasim <- va
```

```{r va-verify}
#| tbl-cap: "The four published years, recomputed against what the report prints"
# Scrape the published tables straight out of the rendered report, so this is
# a check against the artefact rather than against an assumption about it.
lever_html <- here::here("docs", "pulling_the_right_lever_v2.html")
pub_tbl <- function(anchor) {
  h <- paste(readLines(lever_html, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"), collapse = "\n")
  i <- regexpr(paste0('id="', anchor, '"'), h, fixed = TRUE)[1]
  if (i < 0) return(NULL)
  s <- substr(h, i, i + 30000L)
  s <- substr(s, 1, regexpr("</table>", s, fixed = TRUE)[1])
  body <- substr(s, regexpr("<tbody>", s, fixed = TRUE)[1], nchar(s))
  purrr::map_dfr(regmatches(body, gregexpr("<tr[^>]*>.*?</tr>", body))[[1]], function(r) {
    td <- gsub("<[^>]+>", "", regmatches(r, gregexpr("<td[^>]*>.*?</td>", r))[[1]])
    td <- trimws(gsub("&nbsp;|&minus;|&#8722;", " ", td))
    if (length(td) < 7) return(NULL)
    tibble(School = gsub("&#39;", "'", td[2]),
           Year = c("2021-22", "2022-23", "2023-24", "2024-25"),
           published = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(td[3:6])))
  })
}

cmp_pub <- function(anchor, group) {
  p <- pub_tbl(anchor)
  if (is.null(p)) return(NULL)
  col <- paste0("va_", VA_GROUPS[[group]])
  m <- va |> filter(LANAME == "Brighton and Hove", !is.na(.data[[col]])) |>
    transmute(School = SCHNAME, Year = year_label, mine = round(.data[[col]], 1))
  d <- inner_join(p, m, by = c("School", "Year"))
  tibble(Table = anchor, Group = group, `School-years compared` = nrow(d),
         `Largest difference` = sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(d$published - d$mine))))
}

bind_rows(cmp_pub("tbl-league-all", "all"),
          cmp_pub("tbl-league-dis", "disadvantaged"))
```

Both published tables come back **exactly**. The fifth year is on the same
yardstick as the four already in print.

## The league tables as a picture

The tables above are hard to read as trajectories. These are the same numbers
plotted, one panel per school, with a **three-year moving average** through
them — centred where there are years either side, and trailing at the ends —
to take out some of the year-to-year cohort noise.

A single year's figure for one group in one school rests on a small number of
children. The smoothed line is the better guide to direction; the points are
what actually happened.

```{r league-plot-data}
bh_long <- va |>
  filter(LANAME == "Brighton and Hove") |>
  select(SCHNAME, year_label,
         `All pupils` = va_ATT8SCR,
         Disadvantaged = va_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
         `Not disadvantaged` = va_ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(SCHNAME, year_label),
                      names_to = "Group", values_to = "va") |>
  filter(!is.na(va)) |>
  mutate(School = shorten(gsub("&#39;", "'", SCHNAME)),
         yr = as.integer(substr(year_label, 1, 4)) + 1L,
         Group = factor(Group, c("All pupils", "Disadvantaged",
                                 "Not disadvantaged")))

# Centred three-year mean, trailing where a neighbour is missing, so the
# first and last years still get a value rather than a gap.
roll3 <- function(x) {
  n <- length(x)
  vapply(seq_len(n), function(i)
    mean(x[max(1, i - 1):min(n, i + 1)], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
}

bh_long <- bh_long |>
  arrange(School, Group, yr) |>
  group_by(School, Group) |>
  mutate(smooth = roll3(va)) |>
  ungroup()

# Order the panels by five-year mean on all pupils, best first.
# dplyr::pull explicitly - an earlier chunk defines its own pull() for
# reading coefficients out of a model summary, which shadows it here.
ord <- bh_long |> filter(Group == "All pupils") |>
  group_by(School) |> summarise(m = mean(va), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(m)) |> dplyr::pull(School)
bh_long <- bh_long |> mutate(School = factor(School, ord))
```

```{r fig-league-all}
#| fig-cap: "Value added by year, all pupils. Points are the published figures; the line is a three-year moving average. Schools ordered by five-year mean."
#| fig-height: 5.6
plot_group <- function(g, colr) {
  d <- bh_long |> filter(Group == g)
  ggplot(d, aes(yr, va)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "31") +
    geom_point(colour = colr, size = 1.7, alpha = 0.55) +
    geom_line(aes(y = smooth), colour = colr, linewidth = 1.1) +
    facet_wrap(~ School, ncol = 5) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8 points above or below expectation") +
    theme_note(11)
}
plot_group("All pupils", PURPLE) +
  labs(title = "All pupils",
       subtitle = "Points: the year's figure. Line: three-year moving average.")
```

```{r fig-league-dis}
#| fig-cap: "Value added by year, disadvantaged pupils. Small cohorts, so the smoothed line matters more here than anywhere else."
#| fig-height: 5.6
plot_group("Disadvantaged", WARM) +
  labs(title = "Disadvantaged pupils",
       subtitle = "Points: the year's figure. Line: three-year moving average.")
```

```{r fig-league-non}

#| fig-height: 5.6
plot_group("Not disadvantaged", "#2166ac") +
  labs(title = "Pupils not known to be disadvantaged",

```

```{r fig-league-compare}
#| fig-cap: "The two pupil groups on the same axes, smoothed. Where the lines diverge, a school is doing noticeably better for one group than the other."
#| fig-height: 5.6
ggplot(bh_long |> filter(Group != "All pupils"),
       aes(yr, smooth, colour = Group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "31") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
```

```{r league-plot-notes}
sm <- function(school, group, y) {
  v <- bh_long |> filter(as.character(School) == school, Group == group, yr == y)
  if (!nrow(v)) NA_real_ else v$smooth[1]
}
```

Three things the smoothing makes visible that the tables do not.

**BACA's disadvantaged line turns over harder than any other in the city.** Smoothed,
it runs `r fmt(sm("BACA", "Disadvantaged", 2024), 1)` in 2024 and
`r fmt(sm("BACA", "Disadvantaged", 2026), 1)` by 2026 — and because the
moving average is pulled down by a single year, even the smoothed line
understates how abrupt the drop is in the raw points.

**Longhill is the mirror image on the same measure**, climbing from
`r fmt(sm("Longhill", "Disadvantaged", 2022), 1)` to
`r fmt(sm("Longhill", "Disadvantaged", 2026), 1)` while its all-pupil line
stays flat and negative. The all-pupil figure is hiding this.

**Patcham is the school the smoothing helps most.** Its 2023/24 disadvantaged
figure is an extreme single-year value; the moving average shows a school
consistently below expectation rather than one that collapsed in one year.

## BACA, by pupil group

The disadvantaged table is where the year lands hardest, and it is worth
setting the raw scores beside the value added rather than reading either
alone.

```{r baca-groups}
#| tbl-cap: "BACA: Attainment 8 and value added, by pupil group"
baca <- va |> filter(grepl("^Brighton Aldridge", SCHNAME)) |>
  transmute(Year = year_label,
            `A8 all` = ATT8SCR, `VA all` = round(va_ATT8SCR, 1),
            `A8 disadvantaged` = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
            `VA disadvantaged` = round(va_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A, 1),
            `A8 other` = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A,
            `VA other` = round(va_ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, 1)) |>

baca
```

```{r baca-plot}
#| fig-cap: "BACA: value added by pupil group, against the rest of the city"
#| fig-height: 3.8
bh_groups <- va |>
  filter(LANAME == "Brighton and Hove") |>
  select(SCHNAME, year_label,
         Disadvantaged = va_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
         `Not disadvantaged` = va_ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Disadvantaged, `Not disadvantaged`),
                      names_to = "Group", values_to = "va") |>
  filter(!is.na(va)) |>
  mutate(is_baca = grepl("^Brighton Aldridge", SCHNAME),
         yr = as.integer(substr(year_label, 1, 4)) + 1L)

ggplot(bh_groups, aes(yr, va, group = SCHNAME)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "31") +
  geom_line(data = filter(bh_groups, !is_baca), colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_line(data = filter(bh_groups, is_baca), colour = WARM, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = filter(bh_groups, is_baca), colour = WARM, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Group) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8 points above or below expectation",

       subtitle = "Each grey line is another Brighton and Hove school") +
  theme_note(12)
```

```{r baca-nums}
b <- function(y, col) baca[[col]][baca$Year == y]
```

Read across the groups, the year separates cleanly.

**BACA's non-disadvantaged pupils had a good year.** Attainment 8
`r sprintf("%.1f", b("2024-25", "A8 other"))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", b("2025-26", "A8 other"))`, value added
`r fmt(b("2024-25", "VA other"), 1)` to `r fmt(b("2025-26", "VA other"), 1)` —
back above expectation.

**Its disadvantaged pupils did not.** Attainment 8
`r sprintf("%.1f", b("2024-25", "A8 disadvantaged"))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", b("2025-26", "A8 disadvantaged"))`, and value added
**`r fmt(b("2024-25", "VA disadvantaged"), 1)` to
`r fmt(b("2025-26", "VA disadvantaged"), 1)`** — a swing of
`r sprintf("%.1f", b("2024-25", "VA disadvantaged") - b("2025-26", "VA disadvantaged"))`
points in one year.

And the four years before it ran the other way. On the four published years
BACA was **the best school in the city** for disadvantaged value added —
mean `r fmt(mean(baca[["VA disadvantaged"]][baca$Year != "2025-26"]), 1)`,
and improving: `r fmt(b("2023-24", "VA disadvantaged"), 1)` then
`r fmt(b("2024-25", "VA disadvantaged"), 1)` in the two most recent. Whatever
happened in 2025/26 reversed a school that was, on this measure, doing the
thing the whole *Pulling the Right Lever* argument says matters most.

::: callout-warning
## This is one provisional year, and it is a small group

BACA's disadvantaged cohort is
`r sprintf("%.0f", b26[["Disadvantaged %"]])`% of
`r b26$Cohort` pupils. The composition check earlier rules out an intake
effect and the national peer comparison rules out ordinary noise, but a
single cohort can still be unusual for reasons no published table carries —
and February's revisions have not landed. Treat it as a flag to investigate,
not a finding.
:::

## Longhill, for contrast

```{r longhill-groups}
#| tbl-cap: "Longhill: Attainment 8 and value added, by pupil group"
lhg <- va |> filter(grepl("^Longhill", SCHNAME)) |>
  transmute(Year = year_label,
            `A8 all` = ATT8SCR, `VA all` = round(va_ATT8SCR, 1),
            `A8 disadvantaged` = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
            `VA disadvantaged` = round(va_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A, 1),
            `A8 other` = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A,
            `VA other` = round(va_ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, 1)) |>
  arrange(Year)
lhg
```

```{r lh-nums}
l <- function(y, col) lhg[[col]][lhg$Year == y]
```

Splitting Longhill the same way corrects something the all-pupil figure hides.
Its overall value added barely moved — `r fmt(l("2024-25", "VA all"), 1)` to
`r fmt(l("2025-26", "VA all"), 1)` — but that average is covering two
different stories. **Its disadvantaged pupils had their best year of the five**,
value added `r fmt(l("2024-25", "VA disadvantaged"), 1)` to
**`r fmt(l("2025-26", "VA disadvantaged"), 1)`**, the only positive figure
Longhill records on that measure since 2023/24. Its non-disadvantaged pupils
went the other way, `r fmt(l("2024-25", "VA other"), 1)` to
`r fmt(l("2025-26", "VA other"), 1)`.

So on the measure the Brighton argument cares about most — what a school adds
for disadvantaged children — **Longhill improved and BACA fell**. That is a
stronger statement than the headline scores support on their own, and close to
the reverse of what the raw Attainment 8 comparison first suggested.

One qualification, which §7 sets out. The value added here is built on
Attainment 8 as published, a mean over every pupil on roll. Longhill's entry
rate rose sharply across these two years and BACA's fell, so part of both
movements is a change in who was counted rather than in what anyone scored.
Measured on entered pupils only, Longhill is close to flat over three years
and BACA's decline is steadier and smaller than the headline. The direction
of both survives; the size does not.

## The prior attainment the model wants, and cannot have

The model carries `ks2_c` — the mean Key Stage 2 scaled score of the school's
Year 11 intake, centred at 100. It is the term that stops a school being
penalised for admitting children who arrived behind. For the two most recent
years it does not exist.

```{r ks2-coverage}
#| tbl-cap: "Schools with a Key Stage 2 intake score in the performance tables"
ks2_cov <- tibble::tribble(
  ~`KS4 year`, ~`Sat KS2 in`, ~`Schools with a score`,
  "2021/22",   "2016/17",     "5,617",
  "2022/23",   "2017/18",     "5,684",
  "2023/24",   "2018/19",     "5,743",
  "2024/25",   "2019/20",     "251",
  "2025/26",   "2020/21",     "0")
ks2_cov
```

The 2019/20 and 2020/21 Key Stage 2 assessments were cancelled. **The data
does not exist and will not appear later** — this is not a sourcing problem
that a better download would fix. It is the same cancellation that removed
Progress 8 from these two years, and DfE have confirmed no replacement
measure for either. The EES institution-level file carries a prior-attainment
breakdown for 2023/24 only, for the same reason.

So `ks2_c` for 2025/26 is **carried forward twice** — from 2023/24 to 2024/25
by the existing pipeline, and from 2024/25 to 2025/26 here. That is a real
assumption, and the question is how much weight it bears.

```{r ks2-sens}
#| fig-cap: "How BACA's 2025/26 value added moves if the carried-forward KS2 figure is wrong"
#| fig-height: 3.4
req_v <- c(unname(VA_GROUPS), "PTFSM6CLA1A", "PERCTOT", "PNUMEAL", "ks2_c",
           "ADMPOL_PT", "gorard_segregation", "remained_in_the_same_school",
           "teachers_on_leadership_pay_range_percent",
           "average_number_of_days_taken", "OFSTEDRATING_1", "gor_name",
           "LANAME", "year_label")
mods_va <- readRDS(here::here("data", VA_MODEL_FILE))

shift_va <- function(d, school_pat, group) {
  pp <- va |> mutate(ks2_c = ifelse(academic_year == "2025-2026", ks2_c + d, ks2_c))
  out <- VA_GROUPS[[group]]
  pr <- predict_like_published(mods_va[[group]], pp, req_v, convention = "corrected")
  (pp[[out]] - pr)[grepl(school_pat, pp$SCHNAME) & pp$academic_year == "2025-2026"]
}

sens <- purrr::map_dfr(seq(-1, 2, by = 0.5), function(d) {
  tibble(shift = d,
         BACA = shift_va(d, "^Brighton Aldridge", "disadvantaged"),
         Longhill = shift_va(d, "^Longhill", "disadvantaged"))
}) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(BACA, Longhill), names_to = "School", values_to = "va")

# How much does a school's real KS2 intake actually move year to year?
real_ks2 <- p5 |>
  filter(!is.na(ks2_c), !has_imputed_predictors, academic_year != "2025-2026") |>
  group_by(URN) |> filter(n() >= 3) |>
  summarise(sd = sd(ks2_c), .groups = "drop")
typ <- median(real_ks2$sd)

ggplot(sens, aes(shift, va, colour = School)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -typ, xmax = typ, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "31") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(BACA = WARM, Longhill = BRIGHT)) +
  labs(x = "Error in the carried-forward KS2 intake score (points)",
       y = "Value added, disadvantaged pupils", colour = NULL,
       title = "BACA's result does not depend on the KS2 assumption; Longhill's does",
       subtitle = sprintf("Grey band: a typical year-to-year movement in a school's real KS2 intake (SD %.2f points)", typ)) +
  theme_note(12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r ks2-break}
baca26 <- va |> filter(grepl("^Brighton Aldridge", SCHNAME),
                       academic_year == "2025-2026")
beta_d <- lme4::fixef(mods_va$disadvantaged)[["ks2_c"]]
need_d <- log(baca26$ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A /
                baca26$predicted_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A_va) / beta_d
```

Two different answers, and the contrast is the useful part.

**BACA's result does not rest on it.** For the carried-forward KS2 figure to
explain away a residual of
`r fmt(baca26$ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A - baca26$predicted_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A_va, 1)`,
the cohort's actual KS2 mean would have to have been
**`r sprintf("%.1f", need_d)` points** below the carried-forward value — about
`r sprintf("%.0f", abs(need_d) / typ)` times a typical year's movement in a
school's intake, and far outside anything observed. A plausible error of
±`r sprintf("%.2f", typ)` moves the figure by about
`r sprintf("%.1f", abs(shift_va(typ, "^Brighton Aldridge", "disadvantaged") - baca26$ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A + baca26$predicted_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A_va))`
of a point.

**Longhill's does.** Its
`r fmt(va$va_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A[grepl("^Longhill", va$SCHNAME) & va$academic_year == "2025-2026"], 1)`
for disadvantaged pupils is the first positive
figure it has recorded on that measure since 2023/24, but it sits close
enough to zero that a KS2 error of two points would erase it. Treat the
direction as suggestive and the number as soft.

::: callout-note
## What would actually fix this

Nothing, for these two cohorts. The first KS4 year with a real Key Stage 2
baseline again is **2026/27** — children who sat KS2 in 2021/22, the first
normal sitting after the cancellations. Until then every value-added figure
for 2024/25 and 2025/26 rests on a carried-forward intake score, in this
analysis and in anyone else's.
:::

## What it does to the third policy lever

The simulator's third lever asks what happens if Longhill's value added
doubled, "to roughly where BACA already is with a comparably disadvantaged
intake". That framing depends on a gap between the two schools.

```{r lever3}
BHS <- file.path(dirname(here::here()), "bh_school_system", "data")
pub <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "open_scenarios.rds"))$choice |>
  select(urn, school, pan, att8_pub = att8, va_pub = va) |>
  mutate(URN = as.character(urn))

mean_va <- function(d) d |> group_by(URN) |>
  summarise(va = mean(va_ATT8SCR, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

vacmp <- pub |>
  left_join(mean_va(filter(vasim, academic_year != "2025-2026")) |>
              rename(va4 = va), by = "URN") |>
  left_join(mean_va(vasim) |> rename(va5m = va), by = "URN")
va_check <- max(abs(vacmp$va4 - vacmp$va_pub), na.rm = TRUE)

lh <- vacmp |> filter(grepl("Longhill", school))
bc <- vacmp |> filter(grepl("Aldridge", school), !grepl("Portslade", school))
gap4 <- bc$va4 - lh$va4; gap5 <- bc$va5m - lh$va5m
```

The four-year school means reproduce what the simulator ships to within
`r sprintf("%.2f", va_check)`.

| | Longhill | BACA | Gap |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Four years (as shipped) | `r fmt(lh$va4)` | `r fmt(bc$va4)` | `r fmt(gap4)` |
| **Five years** | **`r fmt(lh$va5m)`** | **`r fmt(bc$va5m)`** | **`r fmt(gap5)`** |

The gap is **`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (1 - gap5 / gap4))` smaller**, and
BACA's all-pupil value added falls from `r fmt(bc$va4)` to `r fmt(bc$va5m)` —
from clearly beating what its intake predicts to sitting almost exactly on it.

## And to the simulator's attractiveness term

```{r mult}
#| tbl-cap: "Attractiveness multipliers under the 'families read value added' scenario"
acc  <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "accessibility.rds"))
fpan <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "factsheet_panel.rds"))
oi   <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "open_inputs.rds"))

w_cd <- fpan$factsheets |>
  filter(name != "Total", year >= max(year) - 4) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(p1 = mean(pref1), p2 = mean(pref2), p3 = mean(pref3), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(oi$attract |> select(urn, name), by = "name") |>
  inner_join(pub |> select(urn, pan, att8_pub, va_pub), by = "urn") |>
  left_join(vacmp |> select(urn, va5m), by = "urn") |>
  mutate(wpp = (p1 + acc$pref$decay * p2 + acc$pref$decay^2 * p3) / pan)

W_SLOPE <- coef(lm(log(wpp) ~ att8_pub, data = w_cd))[["att8_pub"]]
mult_from <- function(d, v) {
  eq  <- mean(d$att8_pub) + sd(d$att8_pub) * (d[[v]] - mean(d[[v]])) / sd(d[[v]])
  raw <- exp(W_SLOPE * (eq - d$att8_pub))
  raw / exp(mean(log(raw)))
}
w_cd$mult_pub <- mult_from(w_cd, "va_pub")
w_cd$mult_5yr <- mult_from(w_cd, "va5m")
bacar <- grepl("Brighton Aldridge", w_cd$name)

w_cd |>
  transmute(School = shorten(name),
            `As published` = round(mult_pub, 3),
            `With 2025/26` = round(mult_5yr, 3),
            Change = round(mult_5yr - mult_pub, 3)) |>
  arrange(desc(`As published`))
```

Reproducing the published arithmetic exactly — the `As published` column
matches the shipped multipliers to four decimal places — BACA's multiplier
falls from **`r sprintf("%.2f", w_cd$mult_pub[bacar])`× to
`r sprintf("%.2f", w_cd$mult_5yr[bacar])`×**. It was by a distance the biggest
beneficiary of a switch to value added; it is now one of several.

::: callout-important
## What this means for the simulator, and what it does not

**The scenario still works.** "What if families read value added" remains a
real lever, and it still redistributes demand. But the *shape* of that
redistribution has changed, and the shipped multipliers are a year out of date.

**The third lever needs rewording, not retiring.** "Double Longhill's value
added" is still coherent. "To roughly where BACA already is" is a much weaker
claim on five years than on four — and if the lever is meant to be about
disadvantaged pupils specifically, the comparison it should make is now the
other way round.

**One provisional year is doing all the work.** Before rebuilding
attractiveness on this, wait for February.
:::

# Who sat the exam, and who was in the room

Everything above compares Attainment 8 school by school and year by year.
That comparison has an assumption buried in it: that the schools are being
measured on the same pupils. They are not, and the published data says so.

Attainment 8 is a mean over **every pupil on roll at the end of Key Stage
4**, whether or not they were entered for anything. A pupil entered for
nothing scores zero and stays in the denominator. So a school's headline
number moves when its entry rate moves, without a single child doing
better or worse.

```{r entry-load}
#| cache: true
#| output: false
ks4_raw <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here("data-raw", "ees", "ks4_institution_performance_2025-26.csv.gz"),
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()), progress = FALSE)

enum <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(
  ifelse(x %in% c("", "NA", "z", "x", "c", "u", ":"), NA, x)))

SPECIAL <- c("Independent schools", "Independent special schools",
             "Non-maintained special schools", "Community special school",
             "Foundation special school", "Converter academies - special school",
             "Free schools - special school", "Sponsored academies - special school")

ent <- ks4_raw |>
  filter(breakdown_topic == "Total", !establishment_type_group %in% SPECIAL) |>
  transmute(urn = school_urn, name = school_name, la = la_name, yr = time_period,
            n = enum(pupil_count), a8_sum = enum(attainment8_sum),
            a8 = enum(attainment8_average),
            ent_n = enum(engmath_entering_total),
            ent_pct = enum(engmath_entering_percent)) |>
  filter(!is.na(a8), !is.na(ent_n), ent_n > 0, n >= 50) |>
  # Same numerator; a denominator that counts only the pupils put in for
  # the exams. Where entry is near universal the two barely differ.
  mutate(a8_ent = a8_sum / ent_n, gap = a8_ent - a8)

dis_sh <- ks4_raw |>
  filter(breakdown_topic == "Disadvantage status", breakdown == "Disadvantaged") |>
  transmute(urn = school_urn, yr = time_period, dis_pct = enum(pupil_percent))

abs_sch <- ees_absence_2term() |>
  transmute(urn = URN, yr = as.character(time_period),
            pa = PPERSABS10_2term, absence = PERCTOT_2term)

ent <- ent |> left_join(dis_sh, by = c("urn", "yr")) |>
  left_join(abs_sch, by = c("urn", "yr"))

e26 <- ent |> filter(yr == "202526")
baca_e <- ent |> filter(grepl("^Brighton Aldridge", name)) |> arrange(yr)
lh_e   <- ent |> filter(grepl("^Longhill", name)) |> arrange(yr)
below  <- sum(e26$ent_pct < baca_e$ent_pct[baca_e$yr == "202526"], na.rm = TRUE)
```

## How unusual BACA's entry rate is

```{r entry-baca}
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton Aldridge: pupils on roll, pupils entered for English and maths, and Attainment 8 measured both ways"
baca_e |>
  transmute(Year = paste0(substr(yr, 3, 4), "/", substr(yr, 5, 6)),
            `On roll` = n, Entered = ent_n,
            `Entered %` = round(ent_pct, 1),
            `A8 per pupil on roll` = round(a8, 1),
            `A8 per pupil entered` = round(a8_ent, 1))
```

In 2025/26 BACA entered **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", baca_e$ent_pct[3])`** of its
cohort for English and maths. **`r format(below, big.mark = ",")` of the
`r format(nrow(e26), big.mark = ",")` state-funded mainstream schools in
England entered a smaller share** — so it sits near the bottom of the
country on this, not the top. The national median is
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", median(e26$ent_pct, na.rm = TRUE))`.

That is about `r sprintf("%.0f", baca_e$n[3] - baca_e$ent_n[3])` pupils of
`r baca_e$n[3]` not entered, each scoring zero in a mean taken over all of
them.

::: callout-important
## Entered is not the same as sat

The published figure counts pupils **entered**. A school can enter a pupil
who then does not sit the paper, and that pupil also scores zero. Nothing
in the published data separates the two, so the entry rate is a **floor**
on how many children contributed a zero, not a measure of it.

That matters most in schools where attendance is weakest, which is where
entry rates are lowest. BACA is at
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", baca_e$pa[3])` persistent absence.
:::

## The same measure, like for like

```{r entry-bh}
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton and Hove, three years, Attainment 8 per pupil on roll and per pupil entered"
ent |>
  filter(la == "Brighton and Hove") |>
  mutate(School = shorten(name),
         Year = paste0(substr(yr, 3, 4), "/", substr(yr, 5, 6))) |>
  select(School, Year, a8, a8_ent) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(a8, a8_ent)) |>
  mutate(col = paste(Year, ifelse(name == "a8", "roll", "entered"))) |>
  select(School, col, value) |>
  mutate(value = round(value, 1)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(School)
```

```{r entry-fig}
#| fig-cap: "Attainment 8 measured two ways, Brighton and Hove. The distance between the points is what entry rates are doing to the headline number."
#| fig-height: 4.6
bh_ent <- ent |> filter(la == "Brighton and Hove", yr == "202526") |>
  mutate(School = forcats::fct_reorder(shorten(name), a8))

ggplot(bh_ent) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = School, x = a8, xend = a8_ent), colour = "grey70",
               linewidth = 1.6) +
  geom_point(aes(a8, School), colour = PURPLE, size = 3.4) +
  geom_point(aes(a8_ent, School), colour = WARM, size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(bh_ent, grepl("BACA|Patcham", School)),
            aes(a8_ent, School, label = sprintf("+%.1f", gap)),
            hjust = -0.45, size = 3.6, colour = WARM) +
  labs(x = "Attainment 8", y = NULL,
       title = "Per pupil on roll (purple) and per pupil entered (orange)",
       subtitle = "2025/26. The gap is the cost of pupils entered for nothing, who score zero in the mean.") +
  theme_note(12)
```

Two readings in this report change once the measure is held constant.

```{r entry-corrections}
bd <- function(y) baca_e$a8[baca_e$yr == y]; be <- function(y) baca_e$a8_ent[baca_e$yr == y]
ld <- function(y) lh_e$a8[lh_e$yr == y];     le <- function(y) lh_e$a8_ent[lh_e$yr == y]
```

**BACA's fall is smaller than the headline, and real.** Per pupil on roll
it fell `r fmt(bd("202526") - bd("202425"), 1)`; per pupil entered,
`r fmt(be("202526") - be("202425"), 1)`. So entry accounts for about
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (1 - (be("202526") - be("202425")) / (bd("202526") - bd("202425"))))`
of it and the rest is a genuine fall among the pupils who were entered.
Its entered figure has declined in each of the three published years —
`r sprintf("%.1f, %.1f, %.1f", be("202324"), be("202425"), be("202526"))` —
so this is a trend, not one bad summer.

**Longhill's rise is mostly its entry rate recovering.** Per pupil on roll
it rose `r fmt(ld("202526") - ld("202425"), 1)`, which is the figure §5.1
reports. But its entry rate went
`r sprintf("%.1f%% to %.1f%%", lh_e$ent_pct[lh_e$yr == "202425"], lh_e$ent_pct[lh_e$yr == "202526"])`,
and per pupil entered the rise is only
`r fmt(le("202526") - le("202425"), 1)`. Across three years its entered
figure runs
`r sprintf("%.1f, %.1f, %.1f", le("202324"), le("202425"), le("202526"))` —
close to flat.

## Three years, England and Brighton

```{r ent-series}
#| fig-cap: "Attainment 8 measured per pupil on roll and per pupil entered, 2023/24 to 2025/26. Grey band: the middle half of schools in England on the entered measure."
#| fig-height: 5.6
ent_bh <- ent |>
  filter(la == "Brighton and Hove") |>
  mutate(School = shorten(name),
         y = as.integer(substr(yr, 1, 4)) + 1L)

eng_band <- ent |>
  group_by(yr) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(a8_ent, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi = quantile(a8_ent, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            med = median(a8_ent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(y = as.integer(substr(yr, 1, 4)) + 1L)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = eng_band, aes(y, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey88") +
  geom_line(data = eng_band, aes(y, med), colour = "grey45",
            linetype = "31", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = ent_bh, aes(y, a8), colour = PURPLE,
            linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = ent_bh, aes(y, a8), colour = PURPLE, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = ent_bh, aes(y, a8_ent), colour = WARM, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(data = ent_bh, aes(y, a8_ent), colour = WARM, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ School, ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2024:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8",
       title = "Per pupil on roll (faint purple) and per pupil entered (orange)",
       subtitle = "Three years is all the published institution-level file carries. Where the two lines part, entry rates are moving.") +
  theme_note(11)
```

Only three years exist at school level — the institution-level file starts
in 2023/24 — so this cannot be run back across the five years §9 uses.

## Value added on the pupils who sat

The value added in §6 is built on Attainment 8 as published, which means a
school is credited or penalised for pupils who were never entered. The
measure can be rebuilt on the entered figure instead. Same specification,
same three years, same schools: only the outcome changes.

```{r va-ent-fit}
#| cache: true
#| output: false
va_in <- p5 |>
  mutate(URN = as.character(URN)) |>
  inner_join(ent |> transmute(URN = urn,
               academic_year = dplyr::recode(yr,
                 "202324" = "2023-2024", "202425" = "2024-2025",
                 "202526" = "2025-2026"),
               a8_ent, ent_pct), by = c("URN", "academic_year")) |>
  filter(!is.na(ATT8SCR), ATT8SCR > 0, !is.na(a8_ent), a8_ent > 0,
         !is.na(PERCTOT_2term), PERCTOT_2term > 0,
         !is.na(PTFSM6CLA1A), PTFSM6CLA1A > 0, !is.na(PNUMEAL), PNUMEAL > 0,
         !is.na(ADMPOL_PT), !is.na(gorard_segregation),
         !is.na(OFSTEDRATING_1), !is.na(gor_name), !is.na(LANAME))

ent_rhs <- paste("log(PTFSM6CLA1A) + log(PERCTOT_2term) + log(PNUMEAL) +",
                 "ADMPOL_PT + gorard_segregation +",
                 "(1 | year_label) + (1 | OFSTEDRATING_1) + (1 | gor_name/LANAME)")
f_roll <- lmer(as.formula(paste("log(ATT8SCR) ~", ent_rhs)), data = va_in,
               REML = TRUE, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
               optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
f_ent  <- lmer(as.formula(paste("log(a8_ent) ~", ent_rhs)), data = va_in,
               REML = TRUE, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
               optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
bt2 <- function(m, d) exp(predict(m, d, allow.new.levels = TRUE)) *
  exp(0.5 * sigma(m)^2)
va_in$va_roll <- va_in$ATT8SCR - bt2(f_roll, va_in)
va_in$va_ent  <- va_in$a8_ent  - bt2(f_ent,  va_in)
va26 <- va_in |> filter(academic_year == "2025-2026") |>
  mutate(shift = va_ent - va_roll, not_ent = 100 - ent_pct)
```

The entered outcome is the **better behaved of the two**: residual standard
deviation `r sprintf("%.4f", sigma(f_ent))` against
`r sprintf("%.4f", sigma(f_roll))` on the log scale. Removing pupils who were
never entered removes noise that has nothing to do with teaching.

The two rankings are close — the residuals correlate at
`r sprintf("%.2f", cor(va_in$va_roll, va_in$va_ent))` — but where they differ
they differ for one reason. The shift between them correlates
**`r sprintf("%+.2f", cor(va26$shift, va26$not_ent))`** with the share of
pupils not entered.

```{r va-ent-bh}
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton and Hove: value added on pupils on roll and on pupils entered, same model, same years"
va_in |>
  filter(LANAME == "Brighton and Hove") |>
  transmute(School = shorten(SCHNAME), Year = year_label,
            `Entry %` = round(ent_pct, 1),
            `VA, on roll` = round(va_roll, 2),
            `VA, entered` = round(va_ent, 2)) |>
  arrange(School, Year)
```

```{r va-ent-notes}
g <- function(sch, yr, col) {
  r <- va_in |> filter(grepl(sch, SCHNAME), year_label == yr)
  if (!nrow(r)) NA_real_ else r[[col]][1]
}
```

Two schools move enough to change what you would say about them.

**BACA's 2025/26 survives the correction.** Value added
`r fmt(g("^Brighton Aldridge", "2025-26", "va_roll"), 1)` on roll,
`r fmt(g("^Brighton Aldridge", "2025-26", "va_ent"), 1)` on entered, against
roughly `r fmt(g("^Brighton Aldridge", "2024-25", "va_ent"), 1)` the year
before. Entry explains part of the headline fall and nothing like all of it.

**Longhill reverses.** On roll its value added is flat across the three
years — `r sprintf("%.1f, %.1f, %.1f", g("^Longhill", "2023-24", "va_roll"), g("^Longhill", "2024-25", "va_roll"), g("^Longhill", "2025-26", "va_roll"))`.
On the pupils who sat it runs
`r sprintf("%.1f, %.1f, %.1f", g("^Longhill", "2023-24", "va_ent"), g("^Longhill", "2024-25", "va_ent"), g("^Longhill", "2025-26", "va_ent"))`,
making 2025/26 its **worst** of the three rather than a recovery. Its entry
rate went 91.4% to 98.1% across those years, so the pupils it added back to
the count were ones it had previously not entered.

::: callout-warning
This is a different model from §6 — three years rather than five, the core
specification, fitted separately for each outcome. The levels are not
comparable with the league tables there; only the comparison between the two
columns is.
:::

## What a low entry rate is telling you

A school entering fewer of its pupils is not usually making an administrative
choice. The published data lets this be checked directly: entry rates from
the Key Stage 4 file, special educational needs from the school-level SEN
release, absence from the absence release.

```{r entry-why}
#| tbl-cap: "England 2025/26, schools grouped by the share of their cohort not entered for English and maths"
sen_raw <- readr::read_csv(
  unz(here::here("data-raw", "ees", "sen_school_level_2025-26.zip"),
      "supporting-files/School level underlying data 2026.csv"),
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()), progress = FALSE)

sen_sch <- sen_raw |>
  transmute(urn = URN, sen_n = enum(SEN_support), ehcp_n = enum(EHC_plan),
            tot = enum(total_pupils)) |>
  filter(!is.na(urn), !is.na(tot), tot > 0) |>
  transmute(urn, sen_pct = 100 * sen_n / tot, ehcp_pct = 100 * ehcp_n / tot)

why <- e26 |>
  inner_join(sen_sch, by = "urn") |>
  filter(!is.na(dis_pct), !is.na(pa), !is.na(ehcp_pct)) |>
  mutate(not_ent = 100 - ent_pct,
         Band = cut(not_ent, c(-Inf, 1, 2, 5, 10, Inf),
                    labels = c("under 1%", "1-2%", "2-5%", "5-10%", "10% and over")))

why |> group_by(`Not entered` = Band) |>
  summarise(Schools = n(),
            `Disadvantaged %` = round(mean(dis_pct), 1),
            `EHC plan %` = round(mean(ehcp_pct), 1),
            `SEN support %` = round(mean(sen_pct), 1),
            `Persistently absent %` = round(mean(pa), 1),
            `Attainment 8` = round(mean(a8), 1), .groups = "drop")
```

Every column rises together. Schools that enter nearly everyone have a
quarter of their pupils disadvantaged and one in thirty-three on an
education, health and care plan. Schools leaving more than one pupil in ten
unentered have `r sprintf("%.0f%%", mean(why$dis_pct[why$Band == "10% and over"], na.rm = TRUE))`
disadvantaged, twice the rate of plans, and a third of the school
persistently absent.

```{r entry-model}
#| tbl-cap: "What predicts the share of a cohort left unentered"
mw <- lm(not_ent ~ dis_pct + pa + ehcp_pct + sen_pct, data = why)
broom_like <- data.frame(
  Term = c("Disadvantaged %", "Persistently absent %", "EHC plan %",
           "SEN support %"),
  Estimate = round(coef(mw)[-1], 4),
  `Std. error` = round(summary(mw)$coefficients[-1, 2], 4),
  p = format.pval(summary(mw)$coefficients[-1, 4], digits = 2, eps = 1e-4),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
broom_like
```

Put together, **absence and education, health and care plans are what carry
it**; the disadvantage and SEN-support terms stop mattering once those two
are in. The model explains `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * summary(mw)$r.squared)`
of the variation, so most of what decides a school's entry rate is still
local to that school — but the part that is predictable is predictable from
statutory need and from children not being in the building.

```{r entry-extreme}
extreme <- va26 |> arrange(desc(shift)) |> slice(1)
```

::: key-finding
A pupil who is not entered is almost never a pupil who could have been
entered and was not bothered with. They are disproportionately children with
an education, health and care plan, and children who have not been in school
enough to sit anything. **Attainment 8 counts them as a zero and says
nothing about why.**
:::

The extreme case in England makes the point better than any argument. One
school — `r extreme$SCHNAME`, in `r extreme$LANAME` — enters
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", extreme$ent_pct)` of its cohort for English and maths
and scores `r sprintf("%.1f", extreme$va_roll)` on value added as
conventionally measured. On the pupils who actually sat, it scores
`r fmt(extreme$va_ent, 1)`. Nothing about the teaching changed between those
two numbers.

# What this says about reading a school by its headline

The entry gap is a small correction for most schools and a large one for a
few. What moves Attainment 8 far more than either is something no league
table puts next to it.

```{r absence-bands}
#| tbl-cap: "Attainment 8 by how much of the school is persistently absent, England, 2025/26"
ab <- e26 |> filter(!is.na(pa), !is.na(dis_pct)) |>
  mutate(Band = cut(pa, c(-Inf, 10, 20, 30, 40, Inf),
                    labels = c("under 10%", "10-20%", "20-30%", "30-40%", "40% and over")))
ab |> group_by(`Persistently absent` = Band) |>
  summarise(Schools = n(),
            `Attainment 8` = round(mean(a8), 1),
            `Per pupil entered` = round(mean(a8_ent), 1),
            `Disadvantaged %` = round(mean(dis_pct), 1), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r absence-fig}
#| fig-cap: "Every state-funded mainstream secondary in England, 2025/26. Brighton and Hove's ten are marked."
#| fig-height: 5
bh26 <- ab |> filter(la == "Brighton and Hove")
r_pa <- cor(ab$a8, ab$pa)

ggplot(ab, aes(pa, a8)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey80", size = 0.7, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              colour = "grey35", linetype = "31", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = bh26, colour = BRIGHT, size = 2.6) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = bh26, aes(label = shorten(name)),
                           size = 3.2, seed = 7, colour = INK, max.overlaps = 20) +
  labs(x = "Pupils persistently absent (%), autumn and spring",
       y = "Attainment 8",
       title = "Attainment tracks attendance more closely than anything a prospectus mentions",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s schools, correlation %.2f", format(nrow(ab), big.mark = ","), r_pa)) +
  theme_note(12)
```

```{r absence-numbers}
hi <- ab |> filter(Band == "under 10%"); lo <- ab |> filter(Band == "40% and over")
```

Across `r format(nrow(ab), big.mark = ",")` schools the correlation between
Attainment 8 and the share of pupils persistently absent is
**`r sprintf("%.2f", r_pa)`**. Schools where fewer than one pupil in ten is
persistently absent average `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(hi$a8))`. Schools where
more than two in five are average `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(lo$a8))`. That is
a spread of **`r sprintf("%.0f Attainment 8 points", mean(hi$a8) - mean(lo$a8))`**
— far larger than anything the value-added tables in §6 separate schools by.

::: key-finding
A family choosing on the headline score is, to a first approximation,
choosing on how often other people's children come to school. The number
is real, and it is mostly not about teaching.
:::

This is the argument *How to Pull the Right Lever* makes nationally, and it
is why that report controls for absence before it ranks anything. The
2025/26 data does not soften it. What the new year adds is that **entry
rates belong in the same sentence**: two published numbers, both ignored in
every league table a parent will ever see, between them explain more of the
difference between Brighton's schools than any plausible difference in how
well they teach.

# Five years of Brighton and Hove, against England

Everything above is about one year. This is the series the new year joins:
the city's ten state-funded secondary schools from 2021/22 to 2025/26, on
both measures, with England drawn behind them.

```{r bh-series}
#| fig-cap: "Attainment 8, Brighton and Hove schools against the national distribution"
#| fig-height: 6.2
bh_urns <- pub$URN

eng_band <- va |>
  group_by(academic_year) |>
  summarise(med = median(ATT8SCR, na.rm = TRUE),
            lo  = quantile(ATT8SCR, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi  = quantile(ATT8SCR, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

bh_series <- va |>
  filter(URN %in% bh_urns) |>
  left_join(pub |> select(URN, school), by = "URN") |>
  mutate(short = shorten(school),
         yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L) |>
  arrange(short, yr) |>
  group_by(short) |>
  mutate(att8_sm = roll3(ATT8SCR), va_sm = roll3(va_ATT8SCR)) |>
  ungroup()

eng_band <- eng_band |> mutate(yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = eng_band, aes(yr, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              fill = "grey88") +
  geom_line(data = eng_band, aes(yr, med), colour = "grey45",
            linetype = "31", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = bh_series, aes(yr, ATT8SCR), colour = PURPLE,
            linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_point(data = bh_series, aes(yr, ATT8SCR), colour = PURPLE,
             size = 1.3, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = bh_series, aes(yr, att8_sm), colour = PURPLE, linewidth = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ short, ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8",
       title = "Attainment 8, 2021/22 to 2025/26",
       subtitle = paste("Faint line and points: each year as published. Solid line: three-year moving average.",
                         "\nGrey band: the middle half of schools in England; dashed line, the national median.")) +
  theme_note(11)
```

```{r bh-va-series}
#| fig-cap: "Value added, Brighton and Hove schools. Zero is performing exactly as the intake predicts."
#| fig-height: 6.2
eng_va <- va |>
  group_by(academic_year) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(va_ATT8SCR, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi = quantile(va_ATT8SCR, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = eng_va, aes(yr, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey88") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey45", linetype = "31", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = bh_series, aes(yr, va_ATT8SCR), colour = BRIGHT,
            linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_point(data = bh_series, aes(yr, va_ATT8SCR), colour = BRIGHT,
             size = 1.3, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = bh_series, aes(yr, va_sm), colour = BRIGHT, linewidth = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ short, ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8 points above or below expectation",
       title = "Value added, 2021/22 to 2025/26",
       subtitle = paste("Faint line and points: each year as published. Solid line: three-year moving average.",
                         "\nGrey band: the middle half of schools in England; above zero beats what the intake predicts.")) +
  theme_note(11)
```

Read side by side, the two charts say different things about the same city.

On **Attainment 8** the schools are spread across the national distribution,
and the ordering barely changes from year to year — which is the point *How
to Pull the Right Lever* makes about the headline measure: it mostly restates
who walks through the door.

On **value added** the city is tighter and the movement is larger. A school
can sit in the bottom quarter of England on Attainment 8 and still be adding
what its intake predicts.

```{r bh-vs-eng}
#| fig-cap: "The city against England, both measures, pupil-weighted"
#| fig-height: 3.6
wmean <- function(x, w) sum(x * w, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(w[!is.na(x)], na.rm = TRUE)

agg <- bind_rows(
  va |> mutate(grp = ifelse(URN %in% bh_urns, "Brighton and Hove", "Rest of England")),
) |>
  group_by(grp, academic_year) |>
  summarise(att8 = wmean(ATT8SCR, TPUP), va = wmean(va_ATT8SCR, TPUP),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(att8, va), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("att8", "va"),
                          c("Attainment 8", "Value added"))) |>
  arrange(grp, measure, yr) |>
  group_by(grp, measure) |>
  mutate(smooth = roll3(value)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(agg, aes(yr, value, colour = grp)) +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(measure = factor("Value added",
                                            levels = levels(agg$measure))),
             aes(yintercept = 0), colour = "grey70", linetype = "31") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_line(aes(y = smooth), linewidth = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Brighton and Hove` = BRIGHT,
                                 `Rest of England` = "grey55")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Brighton and Hove against the rest of England",
       subtitle = paste("Pupil-weighted means across state-funded mainstream schools.",
                         "Faint: each year. Solid: three-year moving average.")) +
  theme_note(12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r bh-agg-numbers}
a <- agg |> filter(grp == "Brighton and Hove")
e <- agg |> filter(grp == "Rest of England")
gv <- function(d, m, y) d$value[d$measure == m & d$yr == y]
```

Pupil-weighted, the city's Attainment 8 ran
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(a, "Attainment 8", 2022))` in 2021/22 and
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(a, "Attainment 8", 2026))` in 2025/26, against
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(e, "Attainment 8", 2022))` and
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(e, "Attainment 8", 2026))` for the rest of England. On
value added the city sat at
`r sprintf("%+.2f", gv(a, "Value added", 2022))` and
`r sprintf("%+.2f", gv(a, "Value added", 2026))`.

```{r bh-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton and Hove schools, five years, both measures"
bh_series |>
  select(short, academic_year, ATT8SCR, va_ATT8SCR) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(ATT8SCR, va_ATT8SCR)) |>
  mutate(name = ifelse(name == "ATT8SCR", "A8", "VA"),
         col = paste0(substr(academic_year, 3, 4), "/",
                      substr(academic_year, 8, 9), " ", name)) |>
  select(School = short, col, value) |>
  mutate(value = round(value, 1)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(School)
```

# Where this leaves things

**Settled.** The new year can be added, the new source agrees with the old
one, and the central Lever finding is unchanged by both the extra year and
the change of absence basis.

**Worth watching, not acting on.** On the measure the argument cares about
most — what a school adds for disadvantaged children — Longhill improved and
BACA fell, and BACA's fall reverses four years in which it was the best
school in the city on that measure. Both sit on one provisional year, and §7
shows that part of both movements is entry rates rather than attainment.

**The finding worth taking further.** Attainment 8 is a mean over every pupil
on roll, so a school's headline moves when its entry rate moves and when its
attendance moves, without anyone teaching better or worse. Across England
the correlation between Attainment 8 and the share of pupils persistently
absent is −0.79, and the spread from the least absent schools to the most is
34 points — larger than anything the value-added tables here separate schools
by. Entry rates and attendance are both published, both ignored by every
league table a family will see, and between them they explain more of the
difference between Brighton's schools than any plausible difference in
teaching. That belongs in the main report, not in an addendum, and it is the
strongest argument in this document for the case *How to Pull the Right
Lever* already makes.

**Deliberately not done.** Three things this addendum stops short of, each
for the same reason:

- *The main report is not revised.* [*How to Pull the Right
  Lever*](pulling_the_right_lever_v2.html) still stands on four years. Its
  league tables, its coefficients and its conclusions are untouched.
- *The simulator is not rebuilt.* The shipped attractiveness multipliers are
  a year out of date, and the third policy lever's "roughly where BACA
  already is" no longer holds as stated — but rebuilding on a provisional
  year would be the wrong move.
- *The published panel is not replaced.* `data/panel_data.rds` is untouched,
  so every published figure still reproduces from exactly the files it was
  built on. The five-year panel is written separately to
  `data/panel_data_5yr.rds`.

**What would change that.** February 2027, when 2025/26 is revised and the
full-year absence series catches up. At that point three decisions become
live: whether to fold this year into the main report, whether to rebuild the
simulator's attractiveness on five years, and whether to adopt the **revised**
2024/25 figures EES now carries in place of the provisional ones the
published analysis used — a difference of about 0.12 Attainment 8 points.

One loose end worth closing sooner: the **two conventions** for the residual
described in §6. The report and the simulator currently print slightly
different numbers for the same measure, and that is worth reconciling whoever
wins.
